title: feat(core): plugin architecture overhaul
body:
## Summary / 摘要

Upgrade the `core` plugin architecture from static-only composition to lifecycle-aware, runtime-manageable plugins with dependency ordering, command/event buses, structured diagnostics, and setup-scoped facades; preserve backward compatibility and add runtime-focused plugin tests.

## Motivation / 背景与动机

This branch delivers the plugin-system evolution needed for roadmap-level ecosystem goals (event bus + hot-reload direction) while keeping existing plugins working unchanged. It addresses limitations of static-only plugin aggregation by introducing deterministic plugin ordering, runtime activation/deactivation/reload APIs, and stronger diagnostics/ownership boundaries.

- Issue: N/A
- Roadmap (docs/ROADMAP.md):
  - #9 Widget API standardization (`core`)
  - #10 Plugin event bus (`core`)
  - #11 Plugin hot-reload (`core`)
- OpenSpec change: `update-plugin-architecture-runtime`

## Changes / 变更内容

- `packages/core`:
  - Added lifecycle setup support for plugins (`setup(context)`).
  - Added dependency ordering via `dependsOn`.
  - Added command bus + plugin event bus APIs on `EditorAPI`.
  - Added structured plugin diagnostics querying/reporting.
  - Added runtime plugin management APIs:
    - `getActivePlugins()`
    - `usePlugin(plugin)`
    - `unusePlugin(name)`
    - `reloadPlugin(name, nextPlugin?)`
  - Added setup-scoped context facades:
    - `commandBus`
    - `eventBus`
    - `diagnostics`
  - Added setup-owned resource auto cleanup (commands + event listeners).
  - Fixed missing-dependency diagnostics edge case for single-plugin input.

- `packages/plugin-wordcount`:
  - Migrated to lifecycle-based attach path (legacy attach helper remains compatible).
  - Added runtime plugin coverage:
    - activate via `usePlugin`
    - unload cleanup via `unusePlugin` (status bar removal)

- `apps/electron-demo`:
  - Removed manual wordcount attach and use lifecycle path.

- `openspec/`:
  - Added architecture-level change set:
    - `openspec/changes/update-plugin-architecture-runtime/proposal.md`
    - `openspec/changes/update-plugin-architecture-runtime/tasks.md`
    - `openspec/changes/update-plugin-architecture-runtime/specs/plugins/spec.md`

## Testing / 测试

- [x] `pnpm test` passes / 全绿
- [x] Affected packages build (`pnpm build`) / 受影响包构建通过
  - `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-core build`
  - `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-plugin-wordcount build`
- [x] New / updated vitest cases / 新增或更新的 vitest 用例：
  - `packages/core/test/editor.test.ts`
    - lifecycle setup/teardown
    - dependency diagnostics/order behavior
    - command/event bus behavior
    - runtime `use/unuse/reload`
    - setup-scoped facade auto cleanup
  - `packages/plugin-wordcount/test/plugin.test.ts`
    - setup auto-attach
    - runtime activation (`usePlugin`)
    - runtime unload cleanup (`unusePlugin`) + status bar removal

## Compliance / 合规自检

## Checklist / 自检清单

- [x] Public API changes update package README / types — 改了公共 API 已同步 README 与类型

- [x] Change aligns with project scope (GOVERNANCE.md §4) / 改动符合 GOVERNANCE.md §4 的项目范围

commits_at_first_review.message:
feat(core,plugin-wordcount): add plugin setup lifecycle in Phase 1

Introduce a backward-compatible plugin setup/onDispose lifecycle in core and migrate wordcount to auto-bind through setup while keeping the legacy attach helper intact. Update docs, demo wiring, and tests so existing static plugins continue to work unchanged.

feat(core): add plugin dependency sorting, buses, and diagnostics

Implement Phase 2 plugin extensibility with dependsOn-based topological ordering, runtime command and plugin-event bus APIs, and structured plugin diagnostics for dependency/setup/runtime failures. Update docs and tests while keeping existing plugins fully backward-compatible.

feat(core): add runtime plugin lifecycle management APIs

Implement Phase 3 ecosystem plugin management with use/unuse/reload APIs, active-plugin introspection, and runtime setup/teardown orchestration while preserving backwards compatibility for existing plugins. Update docs and tests to cover runtime activation, deactivation, and reload flows.

feat(core): add scoped setup facades for plugin context

Optimize the plugin architecture by extending setup context with scoped command, event, and diagnostics facades, including automatic cleanup of setup-registered resources on plugin unload. Update docs and tests to cover the new context capabilities while preserving backward compatibility.

fix(core): restore dependency diagnostics and align runtime-order test

Ensure single-plugin dependency validation still emits missing-dependency diagnostics, and update the runtime dependsOn test fixture to declare its actual dependency so the assertion matches the intended behavior.

test(wordcount): add runtime plugin activation and unload cleanup coverage

Add regression coverage for runtime plugin management by verifying wordcount can be activated via usePlugin and that status-bar DOM is removed after unusePlugin.

docs(openspec): add plugin architecture runtime change proposal

Add a minimal OpenSpec change set for the plugin architecture overhaul, including proposal, implementation tasks, and plugins spec deltas covering lifecycle setup, dependency ordering, runtime plugin management, buses, diagnostics, and backward compatibility.

@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+# Change: Update plugin architecture with lifecycle, runtime management, and diagnostics
+
+## Why
+
+The existing plugin model in `@floatboat/nexus-core` was primarily static: plugins were aggregated at editor creation time, with limited runtime control and no structured dependency/runtime diagnostics. This made it difficult to:
+
+- manage plugin lifecycle cleanly (setup/teardown ownership),
+- enable/disable/reload plugins at runtime for host apps,
+- coordinate plugins with deterministic dependency ordering, and
+- debug plugin conflicts and runtime failures in a host-safe way.
+
+To support roadmap plugin-system goals (event bus + hot-reload direction), the core plugin architecture needs an explicit lifecycle contract and runtime management APIs while preserving backward compatibility for existing plugins.
+
+## What Changes
+
+- Add plugin lifecycle setup context and teardown management in core.
+- Add plugin dependency ordering via `dependsOn` with diagnostics for missing/cyclic dependencies.
+- Add command/event bus APIs and structured plugin diagnostics APIs.
+- Add runtime plugin management APIs:
+  - `getActivePlugins()`
+  - `usePlugin(plugin)`
+  - `unusePlugin(name)`
+  - `reloadPlugin(name, nextPlugin?)`
+- Add scoped setup facades in plugin context:
+  - `commandBus`
+  - `eventBus`
+  - `diagnostics`
+- Keep existing static plugin fields fully compatible (`shortcuts`, `commands`, `handlers`, `remarkPlugins`, `cmExtensions`, `widgets`).
+- Add/expand regression tests in `core` and `plugin-wordcount` for lifecycle and runtime plugin flows.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Affected specs:
+  - `plugins` (new requirements for lifecycle/runtime management and diagnostics)
+- Affected code:
+  - `packages/core/src/types.ts`
+  - `packages/core/src/editor.ts`
+  - `packages/core/src/index.ts`
+  - `packages/core/test/editor.test.ts`
+  - `packages/plugin-wordcount/src/plugin.ts`
+  - `packages/plugin-wordcount/test/plugin.test.ts`
+  - `apps/electron-demo/src/renderer/editor-shell.ts`
+  - `README.md`, `README.zh.md`, `packages/core/README.md`, `packages/plugin-wordcount/README.md`

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Plugins SHALL support setup lifecycle context
+
+`NexusPlugin` SHALL support an optional `setup(context)` lifecycle hook. The setup context MUST provide plugin identity, editor handle access, teardown registration, and scoped facades for command bus, event bus, and diagnostics reporting.
+
+#### Scenario: setup hook receives scoped context
+- **WHEN** a plugin defines `setup(context)`
+- **THEN** the plugin SHALL receive `pluginName`, `editor`, `onDispose`, `commandBus`, `eventBus`, and `diagnostics`
+
+#### Scenario: setup teardown runs on plugin deactivation
+- **WHEN** a plugin registers cleanup callbacks in `setup`
+- **THEN** those callbacks SHALL run when the plugin is unloaded or when the editor is destroyed
+
+### Requirement: Plugin dependency ordering SHALL be deterministic
+
+The editor SHALL resolve plugin execution order by plugin dependencies declared via `dependsOn`. Missing dependencies and dependency cycles MUST be surfaced through plugin diagnostics.
+
+#### Scenario: dependency chain reorders plugins
+- **WHEN** plugin `A` depends on plugin `B`
+- **THEN** `B` SHALL be resolved before `A`
+
+#### Scenario: missing dependency emits diagnostic
+- **WHEN** a plugin depends on a plugin that is not present
+- **THEN** a warning diagnostic SHALL be recorded with a missing-dependency code
+
+#### Scenario: dependency cycle emits diagnostic and fallback
+- **WHEN** a cycle exists in dependency declarations
+- **THEN** an error diagnostic SHALL be recorded
+- **AND** plugin order resolution SHALL fall back to registration order
+
+### Requirement: Runtime plugin management SHALL be available
+
+The editor API SHALL support runtime plugin lifecycle management through active-plugin introspection, activation, deactivation, and reload operations.
+
+#### Scenario: runtime plugin activation
+- **WHEN** the host calls `usePlugin(plugin)`
+- **THEN** the plugin SHALL be activated and included in active plugin list
+
+#### Scenario: runtime plugin deactivation
+- **WHEN** the host calls `unusePlugin(name)` for an active plugin
+- **THEN** the plugin SHALL be deactivated
+- **AND** setup-owned runtime resources SHALL be cleaned up
+
+#### Scenario: runtime plugin reload
+- **WHEN** the host calls `reloadPlugin(name, nextPlugin?)`
+- **THEN** the target plugin SHALL be deactivated and reactivated with replacement definition when provided
+
+### Requirement: Command and plugin-event buses SHALL be exposed
+
+The editor API SHALL provide command and plugin-event bus operations for runtime orchestration, and setup-scoped bus facades SHALL be available for plugin-local ownership.
+
+#### Scenario: runtime command registration and execution
+- **WHEN** a plugin registers a command through command APIs
+- **THEN** the command SHALL be executable via `runCommand(id)`
+
+#### Scenario: plugin event publish/subscribe
+- **WHEN** a plugin subscribes to a plugin event and another plugin emits the event
+- **THEN** the subscriber SHALL receive the payload
+
+#### Scenario: setup-owned bus resources auto cleanup
+- **WHEN** a plugin is unloaded after registering setup-scoped commands/events
+- **THEN** setup-owned commands SHALL be removed
+- **AND** setup-owned event subscriptions SHALL be detached
+
+### Requirement: Existing static plugins SHALL remain backward-compatible
+
+Existing plugins that only use static contribution fields (`shortcuts`, `commands`, `handlers`, `remarkPlugins`, `cmExtensions`, `widgets`) MUST continue to work without requiring setup migration.
+
+#### Scenario: static plugin remains functional without setup
+- **WHEN** a plugin defines no `setup` hook and only static fields
+- **THEN** its contributions SHALL continue to work as before
